STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large relative to the frame, so about 26 cm.
b) Reference: no fork or utensil in view. The plate spans most of the photo width, and the food cluster is small by comparison, so the plate is not a small one. Taking 26 cm as the width, with the cues agreeing reasonably.
Final width: 26 cm, area = 676 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Cauliflower (pale, mashed/cooked florets, pieces spread across upper-centre): covers roughly 15% of the plate, about 100 cm². Pieces are soft and partly mashed, about 1.5 cm thick on average (mound, peak around 3 cm). Volume ≈ 100 × 1.5 = 150 ml. Bulk density for cooked chopped vegetables ≈ 0.6 → ~90 g.
- Eggplant (dark purple-skinned, browned cubes, lower-centre): covers roughly 6% of the plate, about 40 cm². Pieces about 2 cm thick. Volume ≈ 80 ml × 0.6 → ~50 g.
- Small scattered crumbs (pale, possibly garlic or tofu bits) and a thin carrot strip: negligible, about 5 g combined.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer visible; the plate is flat with food only on the surface. No additional items added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (cooked):
- Cauliflower, cooked: ~25 kcal/100 g (with light oil from cooking, assume ~35).
- Eggplant, stir-fried with oil: ~100 kcal/100 g (oil absorption).
- Scattered bits and carrot: ~30 kcal/100 g.

Totals: cauliflower ~90 g × 35 kcal/100 g ≈ 32 kcal; eggplant ~50 g × 100 kcal/100 g ≈ 50 kcal; misc ~5 g × 30 ≈ 2 kcal. Total ≈ 145 kcal over ~145 g.
